title: Calculus in Neural Networks: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Calculus in Neural Networks: Visual Guide

1. Chain Rule To Graph | the familiar composition dL/dw = dL/dy.dy/dz.dz/dw redrawn as a graph w -> z -> yhat -> L, with every local derivative computed live and checked against a finite difference | variables in a chain of dependence make the derivative a PRODUCT of local derivatives, and a saturated sigmoid kills that product with one small factor

2. Linear Stack Collapses | up to five layers of a[l] = g(W[l].a[l-1] + b[l]) plotted, with g switchable between linear, ReLU and sigmoid, printing the collapsed single map when g is the identity | with linear activations every depth collapses to one equivalent linear transformation; the non-linearity between hidden layers is what buys expressive power

3. Activation Zoo | sigmoid, ReLU, linear and softmax with their derivatives, plus a decay strip showing the gradient factor surviving after n layers | sigmoid's derivative a(1-a) caps at 0.25 so ten layers leave ~1e-6, while ReLU's constant derivative of 1 for positive inputs leaves the signal intact - and softmax is an output-layer choice for mutually exclusive classes

4. Two Paths, One Sum | one variable reaching the output through two routes, with the correct sum-of-products checked against the two standard distractors by a numerical referee | multiply ALONG a path, add ACROSS paths - a hidden unit feeding many units contributes many path products, added

5. Backprop Layer By Layer | a full two-layer forward pass then the backward delta recursion, the five-factor product for dL/dw1, and a cost counter comparing recomputation against caching as depth grows | the recursion and the five-factor product are the same arithmetic, but caching intermediate derivatives turns quadratic work into linear - and a zero ReLU derivative severs the chain entirely
